content:
Here's my full analysis of the incident.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

The support archive uploads are failing because **the backup tool is blindly copying entire project trees, including massive auto-generated directories** that are orders of magnitude larger than the actual source code.

### The Numbers

| Archive | Project Size | Archive Size | Bloat Factor | Dominant Entry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bundle-4471 | 318 KB | **214.9 MB** | 675× | `.venv/` (201.4 MB) |
| bundle-4488 | 402 KB | **96.3 MB** | 240× | `.mypy_cache/` (88.7 MB) |
| bundle-4502 | 275 KB | **151.8 MB** | 552× | `.venv/` (140.2 MB) |
| bundle-4519 | 511 KB | **42.6 MB** | 83× | `.idea/workspace.xml` (39.9 MB) |
| bundle-4530 | 343 KB | **178.4 MB** | 520× | `.venv/` (166.1 MB) |

Every single archive is dominated by one "junk drawer" entry. The transfer service has a **100 MB limit** (104,857,600 bytes), so 3 of 5 archives were rejected outright.

### What's in Those Directories?

| Directory | What It Is | Why It's Huge |
|---|---|---|
| `.venv/` | Python virtual environment with all installed packages (`pip install`) | Can be hundreds of MB — every Python package plus transitive deps |
| `.mypy_cache/` | MyPy type-checking internal cache | Generated on first `mypy` run; purely ephemeral |
| `.idea/workspace.xml` | JetBrains IDE (PyCharm) project state — local index, run configs, etc. | Some IDEs dump enormous XML blobs that are machine-specific |

### The Critical Insight (from the log itself)

> *"Every rejected archive was dominated by a single directory that is regenerated from scratch on any machine that needs it."*

All three of these entries are **fully reproducible**: you never need to back them up because they're created on demand by the tool that uses them.

---

## Recommended Backup Rule

The backup tool should **exclude** any directory or file that:

1. **Can be regenerated from source** (e.g., running `pip install`, `mypy`, opening the IDE)
2. **Is not committed to version control** (these entries are all in `.gitignore`-type categories)
3. **Is typically large in practice** (the pathological cases that kill the upload)

The rule should apply these specific exclusions (and any future equivalents):

| Pattern | Reason |
|---|---|
| `.venv/`, `venv/`, `env/`, `virtualenv/` | Python virtual environments — reproduced via `requirements.txt` or `pyproject.toml` |
| `.mypy_cache/` | MyPy type-checker cache — reproduced by running `mypy` |
| `.pytest_cache/` | Pytest cache — reproduced by running `pytest` |
| `__pycache__/` | Python bytecode cache — reproduced by running any Python code |
| `.idea/` | JetBrains IDE project directory — reproduced by opening the project |
| `.vscode/` | VS Code settings (sometimes large) — reproduced by opening the project |
| `node_modules/` | Node.js dependencies — reproduced via `npm install` / `yarn` |
| `target/` | Rust/Cargo build output — reproduced via `cargo build` |
| `build/`, `dist/` | Build artifacts — reproduced via build commands |
| `.tox/` | Tox testing environments — reproduced via `tox` |
| `.eggs/`, `*.egg-info/` | Python egg metadata — reproduced by installing packages |
| `.git/` | Already version-controlled — redundant in a backup |
| `*.pyc` | Compiled Python bytecode — reproduced on next run |

### General Principle

**Include source; exclude everything that `pip install`, `mypy`, `cargo build`, `npm install`, or your IDE creates automatically.**

The rule could be phrased operationally as:

> *"Exclude any file or directory whose contents can be reconstructed from files already included in the backup — particularly virtual environments, test caches, IDE metadata, build products, and dependency trees."*

This single rule would have saved all three rejected archives (`.venv/` and `.mypy_cache/` would be excluded), and the two that barely squeaked under the limit (`.mypy_cache/` and `.idea/workspace.xml`) would be much smaller and faster to transfer too.

Agreed, that is where the weight is. Decision: dotted directories hold machine-local state, editor workspaces, tool caches and virtual environments, and none of it describes the project or helps anyone reading the archive later. The backup tool skips any directory whose name begins with a dot, which removes the archive bloat at source. Configuration files sitting at the project root are copied exactly as before; they are small, they are part of the project, and they were never the problem.
